entries.tip: As Sheriff or any investigator, post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and immediately when someone challenges or counterclaims you. Keep your last will current with every result. Withholding a result to bait a counterclaim makes your later reveal look made up after the fact.

support.note: Judy (real Sheriff) held back her Erin-Evil result, and her will still said 'no results yet'. She was hanged 8-4 as a fake. Moderator, Judy and Alice all made this point.

entries.tip: When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both results can be true: Executioner and Jester read Evil. An early Day 2 Evil claim on a player who fights hard to survive fits an Executioner push. Don't hang either claimant because of who sounded better or who answered later. Waiting one day costs little, so wait for mechanical evidence to separate them.

support.note: Erin (Executioner) fake-claimed Sheriff with an Evil result on Judy. Judy's mirror result on Erin was real. The town hanged Judy, Erin won, and Erin's revenge killed Alice.

entries.tip: Claim Sheriff early and lead the day with an Evil result on your target, giving one simple, believable reason. Any counterclaim your target makes afterward will look reactive and invented.

support.note: Erin claimed she checked Judy because Judy was 'last to speak, carbon-copy answer'. Judy's late counterclaim was read as fake, Judy was hanged, and Erin won.

entries.tip: Don't fake-claim a role whose night history a living real holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict, especially a protective role. A duplicate claim becomes a 1v1 the town can settle by hanging or shooting both of you. Prefer Vanilla, or a claim whose actions leave no checkable trace. Explain any visit in a way no living player can refute.

support.note: Frank fake-claimed Medic against the real Medic Grace after Mallory's Lookout result put him on Dave. Carol shot him, and his flip settled the dispute.

entries.tip: Keep your votes consistent with your public reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is exactly the contradiction that Vigilantes shoot. When hunting, look for these mismatches.

support.note: Frank called Grace the Katana attacker, then voted No on her. Carol shot him N3, citing this in her will.

entries.tip: Every Yakuza member must submit the agreed night action and Katana vote every night. Restate the exact holder and target in the night chat. A missing or mismatched vote cancels the attack. Build plans that still work if one teammate does nothing, and hand the Katana to the most reliable member.

support.note: Ivan (Pharmacist) skipped blocks N1-N4 despite repeated asks. On N4 he cast no vote, so Bob's kill on Carol never happened.

entries.tip: Stay hidden, and never announce when or whom you will shoot while a role-blocker may be alive. Shoot players whose votes or premises contradict their own stated reads, or who reveal hidden knowledge. Use Basic shots on suspects with no known Defense. Claim publicly only after your shots have confirmed you, then ask for Medic protection.

support.note: Carol hit three Yakuza with Basic shots (Frank N3, Bob N4, Ivan N5), each based on a vote inconsistency. She claimed Day 5, and her last shot landed even though the Katana killed her that night.
Erin held her shots N1-N2, then used a Basic shot on Dave, who started the DM triangle and led the Alice push. He flipped Fabricator, and she later traded for Heidi to win.

history.old: Stay hidden and shoot players whose votes or premises contradict their own stated reads. Use Basic shots on suspects with no known Defense to save tokens for more targets. Claim publicly only after your shots have confirmed you, then use that credibility to lead the town and ask for Medic protection.
history.note: Heidi said 'I'm deciding tonight' on Day 4. Carol (Pharmacist) blocked her shots and killed her. Heidi's earlier Basic shot on Grace's 'my Katana' slip did work.

entries.tip: Never skip Night 1 protection: Standard Defense stops the Katana. Protect likely Katana targets, such as vocal analysts early and then claimed investigators, or yourself if you have been exposed, and keep a token for a later Strong protection. You get no feedback, so never claim you 'saw' a save. Say only that your protection is consistent with the player surviving.

support.note: Grace protected Alice N1 and Dave N2, and both Katana attacks failed. That kept the Tracker alive long enough to confirm the other claims.
Frank protected the claimed Sheriff Alice every night and stopped the N1 Katana.

history.old: Protect likely Katana targets: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. You get no feedback on whether a protection worked, so never say you 'saw' or confirmed a save. Say only that your protection is consistent with the player surviving.
history.note: Dave (Medic) went unprotected on N1 after exposing himself and was killed. Earlier, Grace's N1 and N2 protections had worked.

entries.tip: A visit shows where someone went, not what they did or their alignment. The Katana is a visit from the holder to the victim, so a Lookout watching the holder sees no visitors. That is consistent with them being the killer, not a contradiction. A tracked visit to a claimed patient can't tell protection from framing or an attack. Before calling a result contradictory, check which roles' actions it fits. Killing an attacker at night does not cancel their attack that same night.

support.note: Raised by Carol, Mallory and Grace during the Dave-visitor Medic dispute (Frank and Grace both visited Dave).
Heidi: Erin's shot still landed on the night the Katana killed her.

history.old: A visit shows where someone went, not what they did or their alignment. A tracked visit to a claimed patient can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Before calling a visit evil, check which roles' actions it fits. Killing an attacker at night does not cancel their attack that same night.
history.note: Heidi called Erin's 'no visitors to Grace' a contradiction of Grace killing Dave. It was fully consistent, and the misread helped hang the real Lookout.

entries.tip: Keep the hostile neutrals (Serial Killer, Arsonist) in the suspect pool even after Yakuza die. A Not Evil Sheriff result or a quiet Vanilla claim does not clear anyone. A Katana attack that fails without the attacker being blocked can mean protection, or a target with innate Defense.

support.note: Arsonist Niaj sat as a quiet Vanilla until the final three. Bob and Carol flagged this risk.

entries.tip: Don't douse forever. Douse players likely to still be alive on your ignite night, not likely hang targets or active killers. Count living players each night and ignite once your douses would swing the endgame. Ignite is an Astral Strong attack, so it is invisible to visit checks but fails against Strong Defense. A douse is a normal visit, so don't douse someone a Tracker has publicly committed to tracking.

support.note: Niaj doused five players over five nights, never ignited, and was hanged at three alive.

entries.tip: As a solo neutral, build specific, checkable reads and a believable soft claim early. A no-info Vanilla claim becomes the default hang once Village power roles confirm each other. At three alive, two Yes votes are a majority, so create doubt between the confirmed players before that point.

support.note: Niaj gave no reads at final three and was hanged 2-1 by the confirmed Dave and Grace.

entries.tip: Each day, ask every living player to name their top suspect with a reason, even if they won't nominate. Repeated 'no case, no nomination' is free cover for evil. The ranked reads create a record to check against flips.

support.note: Alice reports this flushed out real cases several times. Bob hid behind 'no nomination' for days.

entries.tip: Don't publicly announce future night targets. It tells the Pharmacist whom to block and tells the killers where to strike or where not to visit. To prevent retrofitting, tell one trusted player your target privately, then post the resolved result publicly at dawn.

support.note: Suggested by Alice (Vanilla). Thin evidence, and it carries an obvious risk.

against.note: Alice announced her checks and Bob blocked her every night. Carol announced she would watch Heidi, so the Yakuza moved the Katana to Dave and killed Carol on N2. The moderator and five players flagged this.

history.old: Trackers and Lookouts can announce their target at the end of the day ('tonight I track X'), so later reports can't be retrofitted. Weigh this against tipping off evil, who can then avoid that player or kill you first.
history.note: Public announcements backfired: Alice was blocked every night and Carol was killed after naming her watch.

entries.tip: Watch players likely to be visited, such as exposed investigators and probable kill targets, so you can catch both the attacker and the protector. Choose watches that can test an unresolved claim. Repeating a watch on a quiet player gives little.

support.note: Mallory's N2 watch on Dave caught both Frank and Grace, which set up the Medic dispute that Frank's flip settled.

entries.tip: Track players who claim night actions, so that a mismatch is informative. Don't track the same player twice in a row unless you expect them to change targets. A no-visit result on a Yakuza who stayed home tells you nothing. Cross-check your results against Lookout claims.

support.note: Heidi and Dave. Dave's tracks confirmed Mallory's and Grace's claims.

entries.tip: Before a dangerous night, put your strongest current contradiction and any key private replies into your last will. Wills only update at the start of the day, so share later discoveries publicly or with a trusted player promptly. Otherwise they die with you.

support.note: Mallory (Lookout). Carol's will explaining her shot reasoning confirmed her reads after her death.

entries.tip: While an unidentified Vigilante still has shots, prioritize killing whoever is most likely to be the Vigilante. Each Vigilante shot on a Yakuza costs you more than any info role does.

support.note: Bob. Carol killed three Yakuza while Yakuza attacks went to Alice and Dave.

entries.tip: After a teammate is exposed or flips, distance yourself. Vote with town majorities, even against a doomed teammate. Don't immediately lead a push on a villager who opposed your fallen teammate's opponent, because that reads as defending the flipped player.

support.note: Bob pushed the hang of Vanilla Heidi right after Frank flipped and was shot that night. Ivan's votes alongside exposed teammates were also flagged.

entries.tip: When a Lookout or Tracker is publicly active, give the Katana to a member with no claimed role and no reason to visit, and kill or block the info role first. A visible visit to the attack target is the main way Yakuza get caught.

support.note: Frank's visit to Dave was seen by Mallory and led to his exposure.
Grace (Grunt) advised the holder keep a low profile on Day 1 and avoid early pushes. Her exposure as holder got her shot.

entries.tip: Keep your own last will in sync with your current public claim every day. A will that contradicts your public claim proves the lie when you die.

support.note: Frank (Fabricator) noted that a Vanilla will against a public Medic claim would expose the lie.

entries.tip: Everyone can see who sent private messages to whom. Publicly acknowledge your private messages and give a short, consistent summary, so unexplained side channels can't be used against you.

support.note: Erin, Grace and Dave report that PM clusters were used as evidence against several players.

entries.tip: Weigh contradictions between a player's own stated premises above awkward wording or a delayed answer. Delay and evasion are concerns, not proof, because framing, Roleplayers and Executioner pushes all exist. Ask explicitly which premise they reject, and resolve duplicate claims with independent visit or investigation evidence rather than speaking style.

support.note: Carol, Mallory, Judy and Heidi. Delay-based reasoning hanged the real Sheriff, while premise contradictions correctly caught Frank.
Erin: separate confirmed facts such as flips from inferences such as PM patterns or claims.

entries.tip: Keep a running ledger of exact public facts: who voted what on each nomination and trial, who sent each private message to whom (sender, not just recipient), each claimed result and each flip. Check every accusation against it before you make it or believe it, because one reversed fact discredits the accuser. Treat a sudden pivot to a concrete accusation after days of silence as a timing signal worth probing.

support.note: Heidi lost her trial partly because she couldn't cite vote data against Bob's framing. Bob went from four days of 'no nomination' to accusing her.
Six players independently said reversed PM senders drove bad accusations. Erin's error cost the Village the game.
Alice, Carol and Grace: tracking who started the PM clusters (Dave) and who echoed his explanation exposed the Yakuza bloc.

history.old: Keep a running record of who voted what on each nomination and trial, and when people changed position, so you can cite it crisply. Treat a sudden pivot to a concrete accusation after days of silence as a timing signal worth probing.
history.note: Erin (real Lookout) reversed who messaged Carol, was disproven and hanged. Alice, Bob, Dave, Frank, Heidi and Carol all said to check PM direction against the ledger.

entries.tip: Explain each nomination or Yes vote in one concrete sentence on the same day. Avoid 'I'll answer tomorrow' deferrals and empty agreement turns. Give a specific read or a question with a deadline.

support.note: Dave reports that vague or delayed justifications were repeatedly read as dodging and drove several executions.
Dave, Erin and Frank: long loops of repeated accusations wasted turns, so each message should add a read or a question.

entries.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil to a Sheriff checking them that same night, even if they die that night. A Not Evil result on a suspected Katana holder, especially the night of a kill, is not a clear.

support.note: Alice (Sheriff) flagged this exception as a deduction trap.
Alice's N4 check on Heidi read Not Evil only because Heidi held the Katana.

entries.tip: Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1 (e.g. 'holding my Medic tokens'), especially a protective role. It marks you as the first Katana target. Signal through your last will instead.

support.note: Dave twice said he was holding Medic tokens. The Yakuza killed him Night 1 and also role-blocked him.
Frank claimed Medic privately and Alice acknowledged it in public on D3. The Yakuza killed Frank that night.

entries.tip: Never speak from your hidden perspective in public. Say 'the Katana kill', never 'my Katana'. Agree on public wording with your team as well as night actions, because one slip gives a Vigilante a free target.

support.note: Grace opened Day 2 with 'Dave died to my Katana', and Heidi shot her that night with a Basic token. Bob, Dave and the moderator all cited the slip.

entries.tip: In the endgame, weigh hard links to flipped Yakuza above unverifiable claims. Such links include voting Innocent alongside them on key trials and receiving private messages from them. An uncheckable claim like Roleplayer, or a result that conveniently explains a suspicious vote, should not erase that pattern. Track voting blocs across trials, not single votes.

support.note: Carol voted Innocent on Bob with Bob and Grace, and both had messaged her. Her post-hoc Roleplayer claim got her acquitted 1-3, and the Yakuza won. Erin also raised voting blocs. Heidi (0.16) cautioned that vote pairings alone aren't proof.
Carol and Erin: the Dave/Bob/Heidi bloc of co-nominations and Guilty votes was the key lead. Erin cautioned to judge each voter individually.

entries.tip: At low player counts a mislynch usually loses. Before voting, count the living factions and ask what each faction gains from this hanging. Don't hang a role-claimer whose claim fits the flips over a minor factual slip while a stronger suspect lives.

support.note: At 4 alive, Erin's Lookout claim matched Heidi's shot on Grace. She was still hanged 3-1 over a PM-direction slip, leaving Carol against two villagers. Heidi also urged counting factions daily.

entries.tip: When you must fake-claim, build the claim from information your team created, such as a fake Roleplayer 'Evil' result on your Fabricator's frame target. Use it to explain your own suspicious votes, then turn pressure onto whoever voted Guilty on you.

support.note: Carol claimed Roleplayer with 'Alice = Evil', matching Bob's N1 frame. She was acquitted, then nominated the sole Guilty voter Erin, who was hanged.

entries.tip: Pair your block with the team's kill. Block the player most likely to protect or shoot, or the kill target itself to stop self-protection. Once the Vigilante is identified, block them every night. You are block-immune, so holding the Katana yourself lets you block and kill unstoppably.

support.note: Carol blocked Dave while Grace killed him on N1. On N3 and N4 she blocked Heidi, fizzling both shots, while killing Frank and then Heidi.

entries.tip: Treat the nomination vote and the trial vote as separate decisions. Yes only puts someone on trial. Reassess after their defense, and vote Guilty only if the evidence supports execution.

support.note: Frank (Vanilla) said this. Thin evidence.

entries.tip: A missing result is not evidence of lying. A role-blocked investigator gets no result and makes no visit. Don't vote Guilty on a claimant only because they have nothing verifiable. Require a concrete contradiction first.

support.note: Alice, Carol, Frank and Grace all said this. The Yakuza pushed the blocked real Sheriff Alice to trial on D3 with no new evidence, and she was acquitted.

entries.tip: Treat a survived Katana attack, and repeated role-blocks on a claimant, as evidence their power-role claim is real. Evil rarely spends a blocker and the Katana on a fake.

support.note: Moderator: Alice survived the N1 Katana and was blocked every night. Grace and Frank read this as Yakuza hunting a real Sheriff and kept her alive.

entries.tip: Don't DM teammates on Day 1. Plan in the night chat. If you must DM, also message villagers, and never repeat a teammate's public explanation for the DMs word for word. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead for the whole game.

support.note: Moderator, plus Bob, Dave and Heidi. Dave DMed Bob and Heidi repeatedly on D1, and they echoed his 'check-ins' excuse. The triangle was named all game and appeared in Carol's and Frank's wills.

entries.tip: Don't all nominate or vote Guilty together on a weak push, especially against a claimed power role. Split your votes or let a non-teammate lead. Once one of you flips, a shared Guilty record hangs the rest.

support.note: Moderator, plus Bob, Dave, Frank and Grace. Dave, Bob and Heidi all voted Guilty on Alice on D3 while every villager voted Innocent. After Dave flipped, Bob was hanged 4-1 on that record.

entries.tip: Save the forge token for a night when the target is actually likely to die, e.g. a target your team is attacking who is unlikely to be protected. Don't let several teammates share the same fake Vanilla claim or will: the first role flip discredits all of them.

support.note: Moderator: Dave forged Alice's will on N1, but Frank protected her. Dave's Vanilla will was exposed by his Fabricator flip, which made Bob's identical Vanilla claim easy to reject.

entries.tip: Treat a failed Katana attack as a sign of protection or innate Defense. Don't blindly retry the same target. Kill or block the likely protector first, or switch targets.

support.note: Heidi (Grunt). Alice survived the N1 Katana because Frank protected her every night.
